gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada keeps its c forms open and its lowercase bulky, a plain sans with a sturdy build. Tilt Neon is the loud one, a tube-like stroke of constant width, while the body font simply gets on with the words.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham feels approachable and current, with a big central band in each line. Tilt Neon above it traces one thick thread, so you could let the body text sit a notch larger to match that weight.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Dense and dark, Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick stripe of lowercase through every line, its curve endings keeping their distance. Tilt Neon is the one for shouting; the body font is the one for steady talking.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Big, bright and built for screens. Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and curves with wide, unclosed mouths, so it holds up even at a modest size beside the tube-like Tilt Neon.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar is a plain sans whose curves leave daylight, like a rope's open bight, under short ascender stems. Tilt Neon's glyphs look cut from equal-width strips, and they sit comfortably above it.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nag: Confident and punchy, Tilt Neon swings a splayed c terminal and a marker-like line of steady weight. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri is the sans that matches its tall x-height while letting each a open its lower bowl.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Friendly, with swagger up top. Tilt Neon wins on sheer presence, with no thick-thin flicker, while Noto Sans Syriac is a plain sans of bulb-like bowls and wide, easy s turns that is better at quietly carrying the text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wes: Tilt Neon sets crossbars at the same thickness as its stems, giving every glyph a stout, cable-like look. Noto Sans Syriac Western follows with terminals held far from the stroke body, so a long passage reads sturdy yet lightly spaced.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog builds a texture where the middle zone dominates each line, with generous gaps left in its curves. Tilt Neon, bent from one length of tubing, stands apart from that texture.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Rounded, bold and unfussy. Tilt Neon feels drawn with one tip, and yet Noto Sans Tagbanwa, a plain sans with open curves and tall lowercase, sits right next to it without any friction.
